sections.body: The sources repeatedly use GPU-compatible representations to preserve interactivity under scale: shader programs map spatial data to pixels, temporal techniques reuse frame-buffer information, crowd rendering compresses impostor textures, and graph visualization uses OpenGL accumulation fields or CUDA image-space transforms.
sections.heading: Section 1

sections.body: The shared concept is not a single data structure but a design orientation: move expensive rendering or visualization work into representations that graphics hardware can process efficiently, such as shaders, frame buffers, compressed textures, image-space distance fields, and screen-resolution accumulation fields.
sections.heading: Section 2

sections.body: The evidence spans creative shadercoding, real-time rendering surveys, dense crowd impostors, skeleton-based edge bundling, and graph level-of-detail. Because the sources differ in domain, section content should emphasize recurring representation choices and trade-offs rather than claiming a unified pipeline.
